    AI Overview
    The last human moon landing mission was NASA's
    Apollo 17, which landed in the Taurus-Littrow valley on December 11, 1972. Astronauts Eugene Cernan and Harrison Schmitt spent over three days on the surface, marking the final human presence on the Moon until the ongoing Artemis program. 
    Watch this video to experience the Apollo 17 lunar landing:
    50s
    Free Documentary - Space
    YouTube• May 31, 2025
    Key details of the last mission: 
    • Crew: Eugene Cernan (Commander), Harrison Schmitt (Lunar Module Pilot), and Ronald Evans (Command Module Pilot).
    • Last Man on the Moon: Eugene Cernan was the final human to step off the lunar surface
      .
    • Accomplishments: The mission featured the longest total lunar roving vehicle distance and returned the largest amount of lunar samples (approx. 110 kg).
    • Significance: It was the first mission to include a trained scientist (geologist Harrison Schmitt). 
    While several uncrewed robotic probes have landed on the Moon since 1972, the next crewed mission to orbit the Moon, Artemis II, launched in April 2026.
